SEC EDGAR · Regulation D · Public domain

Form D Filings

Every private placement a US company reports to the SEC under Regulation D, newest first. One line is one entry — an opening or a later closing on the same offering — carrying the capital taken in at that moment, not the running total.

Read before using
  • Newest ≠ nowRecords are complete through the date above. A quarter has only 75.7% of its entries filed by the day it closes, so the leading edge keeps filling in for months.
  • ~39%of PitchBook-measured US VC dollars. Anthropic, OpenAI and Waymo file nothing — Section 4(a)(2) requires no notice.
  • 18.6%of entries carry a named investor-affiliated director. Investors are inferred from board seats; no fund is ever named on a Form D.
  • Median 14dfrom first sale to the filing appearing — but the 90th percentile is 224 days. Late filings arrive dated to old events.

Why event grain

An offering can close repeatedly over years. Collapsed to one row, a seventh closing last month looks like a placement from 2023. Here each filing is its own dated line and new capital is the increment — so the sum over a period is real flow, not double-counted cumulative totals.

Reading the position column

  • opening — the first filing on an offering
  • 3 of 7 — the third of seven closings
  • no new capital — an amendment restating other terms
  • restated down — a later filing reporting less than an earlier one

What is not here

  • Fund names on the cap table — Form D never records them
  • Round labels; there is no "Series A" field
  • Rounds placed under Section 4(a)(2)
  • Anything before March 2009, when e-filing became mandatory
